quest.title: Unwritten Rules
quest.description: You and Paimon both hope to see Ginette's research bear fruit. However, the actors in this play turn out to be much more than they seem...
quest.rewards_formatted: Mora x20000, Adventurer's Experience x2, Wanderer's Advice x4

talks.objective: Talk to Ginette and find out what's going on

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, now that Paimon thinks about it, we still don't know what happened to the robots once they got all fixed up. Let's go ask Ginette!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what's going on over there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's crowded around, and then there's Gaudenty...

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: Gaudenty tried to steal the robots I made! If Ineffa and Sarin hadn't tipped me off...

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Steal? Nonsense, I was just trying to see if they were worth investing in!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Analysis of your history renders your current claims difficult to believe.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: My... history? Don't spout rubbish...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino values all items in her workshop, and has established a comprehensive surveillance system through her robots.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: It is almost impossible for an outsider to steal from the workshop without being detected, unless the culprit is assisted from within.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you don't mean...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: While I was here, I swept every corner of the workshop meticulously. As expected, I discovered a few destroyed surveillance robots.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I had Aino repair them. The recovered records make it clear that the "assistant" we are looking for is indeed Gaudenty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he's been working with that receptionist all along?

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: You two were attacked when retrieving the last of the robots, right? I'm afraid those assailants may also have ties to him.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: I... I'm an expatriate representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau! You have no right to lay your hands on me!

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Give it up. You think we haven't figured out who you are? You're no "representative" of anything.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: This man was once a member of the Adventurers' Guild, but was expelled due to misconduct, before turning to bounty hunting instead.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: I've heard that he still hadn't kicked his old habits at that point, which cost him his certification from the Voynich Guild, so now he's stuck scraping by on shady gigs... like this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha! When Paimon first laid eyes on him, she could just tell he was a big, lousy liar! Now, what are we gonna do with him?

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Excuse me. With all due respect, might I take the liberty of handling this individual?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Hey, aren't you the merchant we saw back at the black market?

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: To be honest, there's an unsettled debt between this bounty hunter and I. According to my Agent, he's been hiding in the workshop for quite a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Out of respect for the workshop owner, my Agent never pressed for repayment — so I've come personally to... negotiate this matter in a more civil manner.

dialogues.speaker: Gaudenty
dialogues.text: Asikko, my good sir! Please help me! All that I've done has been to repay the Mora you lent to me!

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Mr. Gaudenty, if I didn't want to help you, why would I have "overlooked" your disastrous business reputation to secure a subcontract from the Design Bureau for you?

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: *sigh*... This was an excellent opportunity for you, but your sheer incompetence forced you to re-outsource the job... to the workshop's owner.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: To make matters worse, you've ignored your employer's demands and allowed decommissioned recon bots to flood the black market... I'm afraid I must re-evaluate your ability to pay off your debts.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The information I have indicates that you are deliberately excising your influence on this series of events.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Oh? How so?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: To my understanding, you previously posted a notice, naming a high price for which you would purchase any of Aino's creations. Excessive amounts of Mora can have a strong influence on certain individuals.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: My hypothesis is that, be it this bounty hunter or the receptionist, their behavior can be regarded as having been "influenced" by said notice.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't stand for such criticism, Miss Robot. From the beginning, I've only done two things.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Firstly, I expressed admiration for the technology Aino has developed. Secondly, I used my own funds to endorse the commercial viability of said technology.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: If greed causes someone to fall out of line, then that is their responsibility to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Indeed. I cannot find any evidence to prove that you directly influenced their actions, and I cannot refute your claim logically. However... there are things in this world more important than logic.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: In any case, I request that you remove that notice. Aino treasures each and every one of her robot companions. We do not desire that a price be put on any of them.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Ah, that... According to my informant's intel, those constructs are, at their core, rather... childish. Hardly something a grown man like myself should find intriguing.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, I still hope to be compensated for my initial investment — just through alternative means. To that end, I've prepared a contingency plan...

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Now, I did not expect others besides the workshop owner to be capable of designing similar constructs, such as this Fontainian engineer. I admire your talents. May I interest you in a potential collaboration?

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: Who, me?

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Indeed. If my intel is correct, then your work has the potential, albeit through sheer luck, to be perfected as a product, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is he talking about the combat abilities that the robots picked up?

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: Umm... I'm sorry, but I'm afraid my work is just as you described Aino's. It's quite "childish," so I doubt you'd be interested...

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: I wasn't thinking about making them into different kuuvahki weapon types while designing them.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: What I wanted to invent was a robot that could use the interactive powers of kuuvahki to gain a certain level of intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: But during my testing, I came to learn that the kuuvahki in the system I designed was not so much "logic" as a type of "emotion."

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: And that's why the robots were more prone to malfunctioning when tests got more stressful.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: But if you give the robots enough friends and let them have fun, the systems run smooth as butter.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: #The combat abilities they awakened were essentially meant to protect their favorite playmate, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: They sound like a group of kids, don't you think? They can't become the weapons you want them to be, because children won't listen to orders.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: Hmm... But there is a possibility, no? Perhaps all they need is to be whipped into shape.

dialogues.speaker: Ginette
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I dare you to try.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Both Miss Aino and Miss Ginette's research has been invaluable to the Adventurers' Guild here in Nod-Krai. I'd strongly advise against stirring up... unnecessary disputes.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Or else, the Guild will have to step in. Are we clear?

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: The Adventurers' Guild... So, you've had an eye on this place then? Fine. Business is business. I'm not in the mood to make trouble I didn't ask for.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: And, as per Miss Robot's request, I shan't make any further commercial demands for Aino's work.

dialogues.speaker: Asikko
dialogues.text: In exchange, I'll take this bounty hunter with me. He'll make up for my losses.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Of course. Please take him away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this really okay, Ineffa? We can't guarantee he wasn't trying to cover for this guy...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: There are many unwritten rules in Nod-Krai's shadows. I do not agree with them. I just don't want them to affect Aino's life.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Some things are best settled outside the workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... If you say so.
